properties.value: Test-fixture key files for the JWT framework's key-loader and console tests; the 3DES is the file-encryption layer (64-bit block, Sweet32), not a token algorithm. Changeable here: regenerate the fixtures with AES-256-CBC DEK-Info.

properties.name: pqs:context

Quantum-safe as a primitive, but a key-distribution risk (any verifier can mint); the HS* analyzers enforce secret sizes. Changeable here.

Quantum-unsafe PKE (Shor) → ML-KEM-768. Ships in the library; consumers enable by alias. Changeable here.

Grover halves the 128-bit key to a 64-bit quantum margin — the weakest symmetric posture in the library; CNSA 2.0 requires AES-256. Changeable here by steering defaults to A256*.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-256 uses: the Concat KDF's digest step (ConcatKDF.php:48, hash selected by the JWE alg), and test computations (manual ECDH-ES KDF reproduction in the X448 test, payload digests in SignerTest). PQ-safe hash; recorded for completeness of the digest inventory.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Concatenation KDF (RFC 7518 §4.6.2, X9.63-style) behind ECDH-ES/ECDH-SS key agreement: AbstractECDH derives the CEK via ConcatKDF::generate; the ConcatKDF utility hashes the input with the alg-selected SHA-2. The KDF itself is symmetric and PQ-neutral — its secrecy rests entirely on the ECDH input (Shor-vulnerable); once ECDH is replaced by ML-KEM the KDF carries over unchanged.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The 'ML-DSA-44 private key' in AKPKey.php is the PROBE_KEY constant: RFC 9964 appendix A's all-zero-seed published test key, fed to openssl_pkey_get_private() solely to detect whether the loaded OpenSSL (3.5+) provides ML-DSA — a capability probe, not a credential (seed is all zeros, published in the RFC). The vectors.json site is the RFC's published key vectors. Hardcoded seed material in form, zero secrecy in substance; key is PQ (ML-DSA-44), changeable here.
